claims.text: Average valence electron count is the primary governor of superconductivity in the proposed single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Average VEC controls the density of states at the Fermi level.
VEC tunes electron-phonon coupling through local lattice distortions.
Replacing Nb or Ta with Ti lowers the alloy's average VEC.
Increasing Ti strengthens electron-phonon coupling up to an optimal composition.
Increasing Ti at the expense of Nb or Ta will increase Tc up to an optimum.
Increasing Ti at the expense of Nb or Ta will increase the upper critical field up to an optimum.
The Nb-Ta-Ti-Hf-Zr family can form a bcc superconducting high-entropy alloy.
High-entropy alloys contain at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
A related Zr-containing Nb-Ta-Ti-Hf-based baseline has BCS-type superconductivity with Tc in the 4.5-6.5 K range.
Related type-A bcc high-entropy superconductors have documented upper critical fields of roughly 9-12 T.
Atomic-size mismatch and chemical disorder create local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions alter the phonon spectrum and electron-phonon coupling.
Ti enrichment causes lattice softening through atomic-size mismatch.
A Nb/Ta-dominated, high-VEC composition has electron-phonon coupling that is less optimized for superconductivity.
Beyond the optimal VEC, further substitution may destabilize the superconducting phase or weaken electron-phonon coupling and lower Tc.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase, disordered bcc alloys without substantial segregation or intermetallic precipitation.
Using an identical powder-metallurgy route ensures phase homogeneity across the comparison series.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows Tc to decrease after Ti substitution passes an unspecified optimum, but the falsification rule treats a decrease during systematic Ti substitution as falsifying. A high-substitution decrease could therefore be both predicted and designated as falsification.
